basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 7.' and it opens 'Vers. 7. Ad fontem Misphat, ipsa est Cades. Cades judicium interpretatur. Ibi enim'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 7. Ad fontem Misphat, ipsa est Cades. Cades judicium interpretatur. Ibi enim judicatus est murmurans populus. Interpretatur etiam sancta cata antiphrasin, id est per contrarium. Fontem petram dicit de qua Moyses aquam produxit. Percusserunt Amorrhaeum qui habitabat in Asasonthamar. Asasonthamar urbs palmarum interpretatur.
